name: Besai
overview: Besai is a male member of the tribe of Levi who served as a temple servant. His role as a temple servant highlights his participation in the religious duties and worship practices centered on the temple. Besai's identity is grounded in his Levitical heritage and his service within the temple community.
namesAndTitles: The name Besai means 'in secret council of YHWH,' reflecting a connection to divine counsel or governance. This proper name, as recorded in Ezra 2:49, does not indicate that it was given directly by God but carries a significant spiritual meaning related to God's secret deliberations.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Besai as a descendant of Levi, indicating his Levitical lineage. Beyond this tribal affiliation, no additional family relationships are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Besai's significance lies in his role as a temple servant from the tribe of Levi, emphasizing the importance of the Levitical priestly class in maintaining the worship and service of God at the temple. His mention in Ezra 2:49 places him among those who returned to Jerusalem, contributing to the restoration of proper worship after exile. Through Besai, the biblical narrative underscores the faithfulness of the Levites in upholding their sacred duties.
